label: early original-phase step just after an n (1-2 steps back)
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at early positions (t=1..4, peak t=2-3) when the letter n was input one or two steps earlier. Strongest when n was the immediately previous input (prev_tok==n holds 85% of activation mass and covers ~98-100% of the top two activation quartiles); much weaker activations when n is only two steps back; the very largest activations come after a double n (n n X). Fires on the token after n regardless of the current input token. Essentially silent in the delimiter and copy phases (even when n is recalled/output), at t=0, and at t>=6; activations die off after t=5, so an n late in the sequence does not trigger it.

issues: Minor numeric discrepancy: the explanation says missed activations hold 0.6% of the mass, but on the test split the misses hold 1.2% of the mass (11,110 steps, almost all with tiny activations around 0.00-0.06 relative to max, scattered across tokens). This is scattered noise, not a systematic class.

The false positives are, as claimed, almost all the prev2_tok==n branch. With prev2==n and prev!=n, precision is 0.71 overall: 0.79 at t=2, 0.78 at t=3 and 0.53 at t=4. The prev_tok==n branch has precision 1.0 at t=1-3 and 0.90 at t=4. So the n-two-back response is graded and weaker, which matches the explanation. Restricting the prev2 branch to t<=3 trades recall for precision: test F1 0.870 vs 0.881. Adding n three steps back drops F1 to 0.779. I found no better predicate.

The claims check out. Phase: original 99.9% of mass, delimiter 0.1% (436 steps), copy 0 activations. By t: 0 at t=0, peak at t=2-3, t=5 rate 0.005, only 50 activations at t>=6. prev_tok==n holds 85.1% of mass. The double-n case (prev==n & prev2==n) has precision 1.0 and about 2.3x average mass per step. in_tok is roughly uniform, so it fires whatever the current token is. On the test split prev_tok==n & t<=4 gives precision 0.98 and mass recall 0.84; t==5 & prev==n gives precision 0.15.
Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.869, R 0.895, F1 0.881, mass recall 0.988.
